Mact, Mandya and M.F
.A.No.6726/2013 arises out of the award in M.V.C.No.168/2010 passed by Fast Track Court, MACT, Kollegal sitting at Chamarajanagar.
Since all these appeals arise out of the same accident, they are taken up together for disposal.

2. On 21.02.2010 when the claimants in both the cases were traveling in bus bearing Registration No.KA-06-A-9236, the said bus met with the accident near Manjunatha Petrol Bunk in front of Mysugar High School, Mandya City.
Both the claimants suffered injuries in the accident.
At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 in the claim petition were the registered owner and insurer of the aforesaid bus.

3. Injured B.Krishna filed M.V.C.No.472/2010 before the Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division),
MACT, Mandya NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and injured Mahesh filed M.V.C.No.168/2010 before the Fast Track Court, MACT, Kollegal sitting at Chamarajanagar claiming compensation of Rs.4,10,000/-.
4.

Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division),
MACT, Mandya NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Both claimants alleged that due to the accident both of them suffered grievous injuries and permanent physical disability.
They claimed that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
Therefore, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are liable to pay compensation.
5. Both the cases were contested by the respondents.
Respondent No.1 contended that the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2, therefore liability to pay the compensation, if any, is that of the insurer.

6. Respondent No.2 apart from disputing the injuries and permanent physical disability of the claimants contended that vehicle was operating beyond permit area and the driver of the bus was not having effective driving license, thereby there is breach of policy condition.

Hence, it is not liable R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
4 to indemnify the damages.
In M.V.C.No.472/2010, the claimant was examined as PW.1, the doctor who treated the claimant was examined as PW.2 and Exs.P1 to P20 were marked on his behalf.

On behalf of the respondents,
RWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.R1 to R8 were marked.
8.
In M.V.C.No.168/2010 the claimant was examined as PW.1 and on his behalf, Exs.P1 to P6 were marked.
On behalf of the Insurer, RW.1 Kaveriappa was examined and Exs.R1 to R3 were marked.

9. In M.V.C.No.472/2010 the Tribunal on evaluating the evidence on behalf of the claimant considered permanent physical disability at 60%, income of the claimant at Rs.4,500/- per month,
applied 17 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.8,26,200/- on the head of loss of future earnings.

The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.14,57,303/- as per the table below:

 5 Towards cost of artificial leg 50,000/-

Towards conveyance, nourishment & 15,000/-

In M.V.C.No.168/2010 the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.75,000/- under different heads as per the table below:

Particulars

R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
5 11.
In both cases, the Tribunals held that offending bus was operating beyond permitted area, there was violation of route permit, thereby there is breach of policy condition.

In M.V.C.No.473/2010 the Tribunal exonerated respondent No.2/insurer and dismissed the petition on the ground that there was violation of policy condition and fastened the liability to respondent No.1 / owner of the vehicle.

12. In M.V.C.No.168/2010, the Tribunal held that if there is violation of policy condition, insurer has to initiate action against the insured, but it is liable to pay the compensation and fastened liability to the insurer.
13. Challenging the award in M.V.C.No.473/2010 the claimant and the owner have preferred M.F.A.No.5373/2015 NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB and M.F.A.No.7246/2014 respectively.
The claimant has questioned adequacy of compensation.
14. The claimant in M.V.C.No.168/2010 has not challenged the award.
Only the insurer has challenged the said award in M.F.A.No.6726/2013 on the question of liability.

15. In the appeals, Smt. Geetha Raj, learned Counsel for the insurer submits that the owner of the vehicle himself has admitted in his pleadings that the bus was operating beyond permitted route,
thereby there is breach of policy condition.
Therefore Insurer cannot be held liable.

16. Smt. Sumanth L. Bharadwaj, learned Counsel for the owner and Sri Raju Bhat, learned Counsel for the claimant submit that to prove the breach of policy condition, RTO has not been examined,
therefore the said contention was not proved.
Under the circumstances, the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.168/2010 was justified in fastening the liability to the insurer and the finding in M.V.C.No.472/2010 exonerating the insurer is unsustainable.

17. So far as quantum of compensation in M.V.C.No.472/2010, Sri Raju Bhat, learned Counsel submits NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB that the doctor who treated the claimant, assessed disability of the claimant at 75% to the whole body and there was amputation of left leg above knee.
The Tribunal without assigning any justifiable reasons has reduced the disability to 60% which is unsustainable.

He further submits that the income notionally considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the compensation awarded on other heads is also on the lower side.
18.
In support of their submissions they rely upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pappu v Vinod Kumar Lamba1.
19. Smt.Geetha Raj, learned Counsel for the Insurer justifies the quantum of compensation awarded in the said case.

20. On considering the submissions of the parties and on examining the materials on record, the points that arise for consideration of the Court are:
(1) Whether violation of route permit exonerates the insurer to indemnify the liability of the owner arising out of motor accident?

(2018)3 SCC 208 R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
6 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB (2) Whether compensation awarded in M.V.C.No.472/2010 is just one?

sentences.text:
Analysis Reg. Insurer's liability:
21.

The parties are not in dispute that on 21.02.2010 at 6.30 p.m. when the claimants were traveling in bus bearing Registration No.KA-06-A-9236 near Manjunatha petrol bunk, Maddur, the same met with accident due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
22.
The evidence on record shows that route permit of the bus in question was from Bangalore to Kanakapura and Kanakapura to Bangalore.
But the accident took place within the limits of Mandya City.

RW.2 the Power of Attorney Holder of the Insured/Owner in his cross-examination in M.V.C.No.472/2010 clearly admitted that the bus had no permit to operate from Ramanagar to Mysore and on that day, the bus was operating beyond permitted route.

Justification was offered saying that another bus carrying passengers on that route had a breakdown, as passengers were stranding, to help them as a substitute bus bearing No.KA-06-A-9236 was sent to that area.
But the fact remains that offending vehicle had operated - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB beyond the permitted area.
The question is in such cases whether the insurer is totally exonerated of all its responsibilities of indemnifying the liability of the third party victims.
23. The law on the point is no more res integra.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in its judgment in Rani v.
National Insurance Company Ltd.2 has held that such violation amounts to violation of the policy condition.

entities.text:
Rani v.
National Insurance Company Ltd.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in that judgment relying on it's earlier judgment in Pappu v Vinod Kumar Lamba3 it is held that the insurer has to pay the compensation and recover the same from the insured.
Therefore in the above cases, the Tribunals should have proceeded accordingly.

Therefore,
the finding of the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.472/2010 totally exonerating the insurer and finding of the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.168/2010 exonerating the insured, was incorrect and is liable to be set aside.
The Court has to follow the principle of pay and recover.

Reg. Quantum in M.V.C.No.472/2010:
24.

To prove that he has suffered grievous injuries and amputation of his left leg, the claimant relied on his own (2018) 8 SCC 492 (2018) 3 SCC 208 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB evidence and the evidence of PW.2 the doctor who treated him.

As per wound certificate Ex.P4 and the evidence of PW.2, the claimant was brought to the hospital with the following injuries:
R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
7 (i) Abrasion over dorsum of left hand measuring 5cm x 2 cm.
(ii) Crush injury over left thigh at the level of middle 1/3rd .

sentences.text: Lacerated wound over back of leg in popliteal fossa measuring 15 cm x 5 cm x bone depth with lacerated wound over posterior aspect of left thigh.
Crush injury of left foot with avulsion of the sole of the foot and heel pad.
(iii) Lacerated wound over upper 1/3rd of right leg measuring 20 x 10 cm with greese mark at wound site.

(iv) Abrasion over outer aspect of right side foot in an area of 8 x 4 cm.
25.

The evidence of PW.2/Ex.P4 wound certificate shows that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
(i) fracture of shaft of left femur at middle 1/3rd, all muscles of compartment was avulsed below mid thigh level with sciatic nerve was cut.
(ii) fracture of tibia and fibula in mid shaft.
26. The medical evidence further shows the claimant had amputation of left leg above knee.

The claimant was treated as inpatient in the hospital twice as follows:
21.02.2010 to 27.04.2010 17.10.2011 to 21.10.2011 - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB Totally the claimant was treated as inpatient for seventy five days.
There was no dispute that PW.2 was competent to assess the disability of the claimant as he was the doctor who treated him.
He assessed whole body disability at 75%.
The Tribunal without assigning any reasons reduced the same to 60% which is incorrect.
27. The Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month notionally.
There was no dispute that the claimant was aged 26 years and he was able-bodied person.
Considering his age, avocation, prevailing wage rates and cost of living during 2010, the income considered at Rs.4,500/- by the Tribunal per month is on the lower side.
The Tribunal should have considered income at minimum of Rs.5,500/- per month.

28. Since the disability was more than 50%, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., v. Pranay Sethi4 and having regard to the age, amputation of the claimant, 40% ought to have been added to his income by way of future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., v. Pranay Sethi4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore his monthly income comes to Rs.5,500/- + Rs.2,200/- = (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 14 - R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
8 NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB Rs.7,700/-.
The applicable multiplier is 17.

Having regard to 75% of the disability, the compensation payable on the head of loss of future earnings comes to Rs.7,700 x 17 x 12 x 75% =Rs.11,78,100/-.
29.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries and period of hospitalization, compensation awarded on the head of pain and suffering is on the lower side.
Awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/- on that head would meet the ends of justice.
30. In view of amputation of the leg of the claimant, he is deprived of enjoyment of life like any other normal person.
Therefore awarding Rs.1,00,000/- on the head of loss of amenities would be proper.
31. The medical expenses is awarded based on records and that needs to be maintained.
32. Compensation on the head of loss of income during laid up period has to be considered for atleast six months at the rate of Rs.5,500/- which comes to Rs.5,500 x 6 - Rs.33,000/-.
33. As per the evidence of PW.2, the claimant had to go for fixing artificial limb.

Therefore compensation of Rs.50,000/-
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB awarded on head of future medical expenses needs to be maintained.
34. Having regard to the period of hospitalization, compensation awarded on the head of conveyance, attendant charges, diet and nourishment requires to be enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation on the head of loss of marriage prospects.
Learned Counsel for the claimant submits that the claimant has not yet married.
Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, awarding Rs.1,00,000/- on the lead of loss of marriage prospects would meet the ends of justice.

Thus just compensation payable is as follows:

 1. Loss of future earnings 11,78,100/-
 2. Pain and Sufferings 75,000/-
 3. Loss of income during laid up period 33,000/-
 4. Medical expenses 4,85,453/-
 5. Future medical expenses 50,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities 1,00,000/-
 7. Food, Nourishment, Attendant 25,000/-
 charges and conveyance  8. Marriage prospects 1,00,000/-
 Total 20,46,553/-
 rounded off to  20,46,550/-

9
Hence, the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,46,550/-.
The said compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
35. For the aforesaid reasons, M.F.A.No.7246/2014 is liable to be dismissed, M.F.A.No.5373/2015 and M.F.A.No.6726/2013 deserve to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER M.F.A.No.7246/2014 is dismissed.
M.F.A.No.5375/2015 and M.F.A.No.6726/2013 are partly allowed.

The award in MVC No.472/2010 on the file of Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division),
MACT, Mandya is modified as follows:
The claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.20,46,550/- with interest thereon at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.2 Insurer shall deposit the award amount in both cases on adjusting the amount already deposited, by it, as well as the insured, if any, before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

.A.No.6726/2013 arises out of the award in M.V.C.No.168/2010 passed by Fast Track Court, MACT, Kollegal sitting at Chamarajanagar.
Since all these appeals arise out of the same accident, they are taken up together for disposal.
3. Injured B.Krishna filed M.V.C.No.472/2010 before the Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division),
MACT, Mandya NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and injured Mahesh filed M.V.C.No.168/2010 before the Fast Track Court, MACT, Kollegal sitting at Chamarajanagar claiming compensation of Rs.4,10,000/-.
4.
opennyai_summary.facts:
Both the claimants suffered injuries in the accident.
Both claimants alleged that due to the accident both of them suffered grievous injuries and permanent physical disability.
They claimed that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
Therefore, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are liable to pay compensation.
Respondent No.1 contended that the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2, therefore liability to pay the compensation, if any, is that of the insurer.
6. Respondent No.2 apart from disputing the injuries and permanent physical disability of the claimants contended that vehicle was operating beyond permit area and the driver of the bus was not having effective driving license, thereby there is breach of policy condition.
Hence, it is not liable R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
4 to indemnify the damages.
12. In M.V.C.No.168/2010, the Tribunal held that if there is violation of policy condition, insurer has to initiate action against the insured, but it is liable to pay the compensation and fastened liability to the insurer.
The claimant has questioned adequacy of compensation.
Only the insurer has challenged the said award in M.F.A.No.6726/2013 on the question of liability.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Under the circumstances, the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.168/2010 was justified in fastening the liability to the insurer and the finding in M.V.C.No.472/2010 exonerating the insurer is unsustainable.
The Tribunal without assigning any justifiable reasons has reduced the disability to 60% which is unsustainable.
19. Smt.Geetha Raj, learned Counsel for the Insurer justifies the quantum of compensation awarded in the said case.
opennyai_summary.issue:
20. On considering the submissions of the parties and on examining the materials on record, the points that arise for consideration of the Court are:
(1) Whether violation of route permit exonerates the insurer to indemnify the liability of the owner arising out of motor accident?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hon'ble Supreme Court in its judgment in Rani v.
National Insurance Company Ltd.2 has held that such violation amounts to violation of the policy condition.
Therefore,
the finding of the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.472/2010 totally exonerating the insurer and finding of the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.168/2010 exonerating the insured, was incorrect and is liable to be set aside.
The Court has to follow the principle of pay and recover.
There was no dispute that the claimant was aged 26 years and he was able-bodied person.
Considering his age, avocation, prevailing wage rates and cost of living during 2010, the income considered at Rs.4,500/- by the Tribunal per month is on the lower side.
The Tribunal should have considered income at minimum of Rs.5,500/- per month.
28. Since the disability was more than 50%, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., v. Pranay Sethi4 and having regard to the age, amputation of the claimant, 40% ought to have been added to his income by way of future prospects.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Having regard to 75% of the disability, the compensation payable on the head of loss of future earnings comes to Rs.7,700 x 17 x 12 x 75% =Rs.11,78,100/-.
29.
Awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/- on that head would meet the ends of justice.
30. In view of amputation of the leg of the claimant, he is deprived of enjoyment of life like any other normal person.
Therefore awarding Rs.1,00,000/- on the head of loss of amenities would be proper.
31. The medical expenses is awarded based on records and that needs to be maintained.
32. Compensation on the head of loss of income during laid up period has to be considered for atleast six months at the rate of Rs.5,500/- which comes to Rs.5,500 x 6 - Rs.33,000/-.
33. As per the evidence of PW.2, the claimant had to go for fixing artificial limb.
Therefore compensation of Rs.50,000/-
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB awarded on head of future medical expenses needs to be maintained.
34. Having regard to the period of hospitalization, compensation awarded on the head of conveyance, attendant charges, diet and nourishment requires to be enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation on the head of loss of marriage prospects.
Learned Counsel for the claimant submits that the claimant has not yet married.
Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, awarding Rs.1,00,000/- on the lead of loss of marriage prospects would meet the ends of justice.
Thus just compensation payable is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future earnings 11,78,100/-
 2. Pain and Sufferings 75,000/-
 3. Loss of income during laid up period 33,000/-
 4. Medical expenses 4,85,453/-
 5. Future medical expenses 50,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities 1,00,000/-
 7. Food, Nourishment, Attendant 25,000/-
 charges and conveyance  8. Marriage prospects 1,00,000/-
 Total 20,46,553/-
 rounded off to  20,46,550/-
 - 16 -  NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB R. Pari vs B Krishna on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151967700/
9
Hence, the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,46,550/-.
The said compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
35. For the aforesaid reasons, M.F.A.No.7246/2014 is liable to be dismissed, M.F.A.No.5373/2015 and M.F.A.No.6726/2013 deserve to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following:
ORDER M.F.A.No.7246/2014 is dismissed.
M.F.A.No.5375/2015 and M.F.A.No.6726/2013 are partly allowed.
The award in MVC No.472/2010 on the file of Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division),
MACT, Mandya is modified as follows:
The claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.20,46,550/- with interest thereon at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.2 Insurer shall deposit the award amount in both cases on adjusting the amount already deposited, by it, as well as the insured, if any, before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
- 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:45908-DB
The judgment and award in M.V.C.No.168/2010 awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/- with interest at 6% per annum is maintained.
Respondent No.2 insurer shall deposit the amount before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order on adjusting the amount already deposited, if any.
In both the cases, respondent No.1/insured shall pay the amount deposited by the insurer forthwith.
In case of default, respondent No.2 insurer shall recover the same in execution of this decree.
Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit and the TCR to the respective Tribunals, forthwith.
